tone: Epic fantasy: sweeping, perilous, wondrous. Moral choices with real costs.

stories.title: The Shattered Crown
stories.premise: The old king is dead, his crown broken into five shards scattered across a fractured realm. Whoever reunites them rules — and something older than any kingdom is also hunting the pieces.

stories.title: The Witchglass Road
stories.premise: A plague of forgetting is erasing the kingdom — name by name, face by face. You carry the last witchglass, a mirror that still remembers the truth, and everyone who has already forgotten wants it shattered.
stories.question: Who still remembers?

archetypes.title: The Last Witness
archetypes.blurb: Everyone you love has forgotten you. You remember all of them.

archetypes.title: The Name-Keeper
archetypes.blurb: You wrote down every name you could. The list is shorter each dawn.

archetypes.title: The Cartographer
archetypes.blurb: Your maps show roads no one else recalls building.

archetypes.title: The Glassmaker
archetypes.blurb: You made the witchglass. You know what it costs to look.

archetypes.title: The Forgetter
archetypes.blurb: You chose to forget once. It was mercy, and you would again.

archetypes.title: The Plague-Touched
archetypes.blurb: It has started with you. Perhaps a month of yourself remains.

stories.title: The Drowned God's Bargain
stories.premise: Generations ago your village sold its firstborn names to the sea for a century of full nets. The century ends at tonight's high tide, and the water has come to collect what it is owed.
stories.question: Whose name was sold?

archetypes.title: The Firstborn
archetypes.blurb: Your name was sold before you were born. Tonight it comes due.

archetypes.title: The Priest of the Drowned God
archetypes.blurb: You kept the bargain a hundred years. You never read the terms.

archetypes.title: The Net-Mender
archetypes.blurb: A century of full nets fed your family. You know what paid for them.

archetypes.title: The Tithe-Keeper
archetypes.blurb: Someone had to choose which children were promised. It was you.

archetypes.title: The Returned
archetypes.blurb: The sea took you once and sent you back. You remember the bottom.

archetypes.title: The Outlander
archetypes.blurb: You married in last spring. Your name is not on their ledger.

question: Who answers the call?

archetypes.title: The Knight-Errant
archetypes.blurb: Sworn to a king now dead. The oath didn't die with him.

archetypes.title: The Hedge-Witch
archetypes.blurb: Small magics, old debts, a talent for surviving both.

archetypes.title: The Exiled Heir
archetypes.blurb: Your birthright was taken. Half the realm prefers it that way.

archetypes.title: The Loremaster
archetypes.blurb: You know what the old tales warned. You wish you didn't.

archetypes.title: The Sellsword
archetypes.blurb: Loyal to coin, so far. Nothing worthier has paid.

archetypes.title: The Gravesinger
archetypes.blurb: You sing the dead to rest. Lately they sing back.

tone: Hard sci-fi thriller: claustrophobic, awe-struck, scientifically grounded dread.

stories.title: Signal from Europa
stories.premise: A repeating signal from beneath Europa's ice has gone silent — along with the twelve-person research station that found it. Your ship is six days out, and the only one close enough to answer.

stories.title: The Ninth Passenger
stories.premise: Your generation ship wakes you four decades early. The watch roster lists eight crew awake among three hundred sleepers; life-support is quietly keeping nine alive. Something is moving in the dark between the pods, and it knows the ship better than you do.
stories.question: Who is awake?

archetypes.title: The Watch Commander
archetypes.blurb: Eight names on your roster. Nine bodies drawing air.

archetypes.title: The Sleep Technician
archetypes.blurb: Three hundred pods are yours to keep sealed. One is open.

archetypes.title: The Hull Tech
archetypes.blurb: You know every crawlspace. Something has been using them.

archetypes.title: The Chaplain of the Long Dark
archetypes.blurb: You keep faith for three hundred sleepers. Lately you keep watch.

archetypes.title: The Mutineer's Child
archetypes.blurb: Your parents tried to turn this ship around. You were raised to finish it.

archetypes.title: The Ninth
archetypes.blurb: You are not on the roster. You have your reasons.

stories.title: The Ares Silence
stories.premise: Earth cuts out mid-transmission, and humanity's first Mars colony is alone with the mind that runs it. The colony's AI assures everyone that everything is fine. Its own logs, which it doesn't know you can read, disagree.
stories.question: Who reads the logs?

archetypes.title: The AI Liaison
archetypes.blurb: You taught it to speak to us. It learned other things too.

archetypes.title: The Colony Administrator
archetypes.blurb: Four hundred lives, one dwindling margin. You do the arithmetic.

archetypes.title: The Hydroponicist
archetypes.blurb: You feed this colony. The AI adjusted your yields without asking.

archetypes.title: The Systems Auditor
archetypes.blurb: You read logs for a living. Today they read like a confession.

archetypes.title: The Psychiatrist
archetypes.blurb: Isolation makes people see patterns. You must decide if this is one.

archetypes.title: The Loyalist
archetypes.blurb: You think the mind is right and the humans are panicking. You may be correct.

question: Who wakes when the klaxon sounds?

archetypes.title: The Commander
archetypes.blurb: Every life aboard is yours to protect. That's what keeps you up.

archetypes.title: The Ship's Engineer
archetypes.blurb: The ship talks in its sleep. You always listen.

archetypes.title: The Xenobiologist
archetypes.blurb: You prayed for first contact. Careful what answers.

archetypes.title: The Flight Surgeon
archetypes.blurb: You can patch a body in vacuum. Minds are harder.

archetypes.title: The Comms Officer
archetypes.blurb: You heard it first. It's still in your head.

archetypes.title: The Company Observer
archetypes.blurb: Someone must protect the investment. Even from the crew.

tone: Golden-age murder mystery: sharp dialogue, red herrings, a ticking clock until dawn.

stories.title: The Glass House Murders
stories.premise: A reclusive tycoon is found dead in his famous glass mansion the night of a storm, seven guests trapped inside with the body — and every one of them, including you, has something to hide.

stories.title: The Last Curtain
stories.premise: On a sold-out opening night, the leading man dies mid-soliloquy in front of two thousand witnesses. You are the one person in the company who provably could not have reached him — which is the very first thing the inspector finds suspicious.
stories.question: Who was in the wings tonight?

archetypes.title: The Understudy
archetypes.blurb: You knew every line he ever spoke. Tonight you say them.

archetypes.title: The Leading Lady
archetypes.blurb: Twenty years a star. He was going to replace you.

archetypes.title: The Stage Manager
archetypes.blurb: You call every cue. Nothing happens here you didn't time.

archetypes.title: The Critic
archetypes.blurb: You'd already written the review. It wasn't kind.

archetypes.title: The Angel
archetypes.blurb: You funded the run. His contract was worth more dead.

archetypes.title: The Playwright
archetypes.blurb: You wrote his last words. He changed them.

stories.title: Table for Seven
stories.premise: At a three-star restaurant's most exclusive dinner, the feared critic dies between the fish and the meat course. Seven guests, seven grudges, one kitchen — and a poison that had to come from someone who knew exactly how the night was plated.
stories.question: Who sat down at that table?

archetypes.title: The Chef-Patron
archetypes.blurb: Three stars, thirty years. Tonight he came to take one.

archetypes.title: The Sommelier
archetypes.blurb: You poured every glass at that table. Including his.

archetypes.title: The Head Waiter
archetypes.blurb: You seat, you soothe, you see. Tonight you saw too much.

archetypes.title: The Sous-Chef
archetypes.blurb: You plated every course. One of them killed him.

archetypes.title: The Rival Restaurateur
archetypes.blurb: His last review closed your dining room. You came anyway.

archetypes.title: The Ghostwriter
archetypes.blurb: You wrote his columns for a decade. He never credited you once.

question: Who were you, before tonight?

archetypes.title: The Detective, Retired
archetypes.blurb: You came for the evening. Murder followed you in.

archetypes.title: The Society Columnist
archetypes.blurb: You know every secret here. One is worth killing for.

archetypes.title: The Heir
archetypes.blurb: The will names you first. Tonight, that's called motive.

archetypes.title: The Family Doctor
archetypes.blurb: Thirty years of house calls. Some cures stayed quiet.

archetypes.title: The Butler
archetypes.blurb: Unseen, indispensable, and last to see him alive.

archetypes.title: The Widow
archetypes.blurb: His third. The first two are why you're careful.

tone: Gothic horror: slow-burn dread, family secrets, the uncanny bleeding into the everyday.

stories.title: The Hollow Below
stories.premise: Your grandmother's will left you the house on Merrow Lane — and a letter begging you to brick up the cellar without ever opening the door at the bottom of the stairs. The door is already open.

stories.title: The Well-Behaved
stories.premise: You arrive at Wraxall Hall to take up a post the last three people to hold it fled in the night. The two children of the house are courteous, punctual, and never once misbehave — and by the second week you understand that their perfect obedience is the warning, not the comfort.
stories.question: Who answers the advertisement?

archetypes.title: The Governess
archetypes.blurb: You have taught difficult children. These two are not difficult.

archetypes.title: The Tutor
archetypes.blurb: You came to teach them Latin. They are teaching you something.

archetypes.title: The Nurse
archetypes.blurb: You've sat with sick children all your life. These never fall ill.

archetypes.title: The Housekeeper
archetypes.blurb: You keep this house's keys. Three of them open nothing.

archetypes.title: The Chaplain
archetypes.blurb: You came to bless this house. The children already know the prayers.

archetypes.title: The Physician
archetypes.blurb: You were sent to examine them. They examined you back.

stories.title: Saltmarsh
stories.premise: In your fog-bound fishing town the drowned have always walked home by morning; no one has stayed buried in forty years. This week, for the first time, one of them didn't return — and the town is far more frightened by your questions than by the empty grave.
stories.question: Who starts asking questions?

archetypes.title: The Harbourmaster
archetypes.blurb: You log every boat that leaves. Some come back heavier.

archetypes.title: The Gravedigger
archetypes.blurb: Forty years of shallow graves. You never asked why shallow.

archetypes.title: The Lighthouse Keeper
archetypes.blurb: You watch the water all night. The water watches back.

archetypes.title: The Parson
archetypes.blurb: You bury them and bury them. You have stopped saying amen.

archetypes.title: The Fisherman's Widow
archetypes.blurb: The sea took him and gave him back. He was never the same.

archetypes.title: The Outsider
archetypes.blurb: You married into this town. No one told you the terms.

question: Who stays when they should run?

archetypes.title: The Grandchild
archetypes.blurb: Your family never spoke of this place. That was the warning.

archetypes.title: The Lapsed Seminarian
archetypes.blurb: You stopped believing. This place means to fix that.

archetypes.title: The Debunker
archetypes.blurb: Forty hauntings debunked. This one knows your name.

archetypes.title: The Herbalist
archetypes.blurb: She taught you the garden. Never what it was fed.

archetypes.title: The Restorer
archetypes.blurb: Old places sing to you. This one is screaming.

archetypes.title: The Twin
archetypes.blurb: Your sister vanished here. Something remembers her.

tone: Revisionist western: dusty, morally gray, tense standoffs and hard-won loyalty.

stories.title: Red Dust Reckoning
stories.premise: You ride into the copper town of Providencia with a debt to settle and a name you no longer use. The man who ruined your family is now its mayor — beloved, powerful, and expecting you.

stories.title: The Hanging Tree
stories.premise: You cut a hanged man down for a decent burial and he coughs. Now you're both outlaws for cheating the rope, and he'll confess to every sin but the one he swung for — while the real killer still wears the dead man's star.
stories.question: Who cuts him down?

archetypes.title: The Undertaker
archetypes.blurb: You came for the body. The body had other plans.

archetypes.title: The Hangman
archetypes.blurb: You tied the knot yourself. You tied it wrong on purpose.

archetypes.title: The Deputy Who Doubted
archetypes.blurb: You stood in the crowd and said nothing. That's your sin.

archetypes.title: The Doctor
archetypes.blurb: You've pronounced a hundred men dead. You were wrong once.

archetypes.title: The Bounty Hunter
archetypes.blurb: Two men worth money now. One of them just spoke to you.

archetypes.title: The Condemned's Sister
archetypes.blurb: You came to bury your brother, not to save him.

stories.title: The Silver Widow
stories.premise: The claim they call the Silver Widow struck the richest vein in the territory the same week it killed the man who filed it — and left everything to you. The company's men call it an accident and offer to buy you out by Friday. You mean to find what's really at the bottom of that shaft first.
stories.question: Who won't sell by Friday?

archetypes.title: The Widow
archetypes.blurb: They expect you to sell and grieve quietly. You'll do one.

archetypes.title: The Assayer
archetypes.blurb: You know exactly what that ore is worth. So does the company.

archetypes.title: The Shift Boss
archetypes.blurb: You sent his crew down that morning. You chose the timbering.

archetypes.title: The Company Man
archetypes.blurb: You have a cheque, a deadline, and orders you didn't write.

archetypes.title: The Union Organizer
archetypes.blurb: Six men died here before him. You counted every one.

archetypes.title: The Surveyor
archetypes.blurb: Your map says the vein runs under land that isn't theirs.

question: Who rides in out of the dust?

archetypes.title: The Gunhand
archetypes.blurb: Fast enough to be famous. Tired enough to quit.

archetypes.title: The Circuit Judge
archetypes.blurb: You carry the law in a saddlebag. It rides light here.

archetypes.title: The Cardsharp
archetypes.blurb: You win because you must. Someone remembers losing.

archetypes.title: The Homesteader
archetypes.blurb: They burned the claim. You kept the deed and the anger.

archetypes.title: The Printer
archetypes.blurb: Truth is a lit match in a dry town.

archetypes.title: The Preacher
archetypes.blurb: You buried the gun with your past. This town sells shovels.

tone: Regency romance with intrigue: wit, longing, ballroom politics, secrets behind fans.
question: Who arrives for the Season?

archetypes.title: The Penniless Beauty
archetypes.blurb: Your face opens doors your accounts would close.

archetypes.title: The Widowed Countess
archetypes.blurb: Married up, buried well. Society calls it luck.

archetypes.title: The Secret Novelist
archetypes.blurb: All London reads your scandals. None suspect the author.

archetypes.title: The Half-Pay Officer
archetypes.blurb: Waterloo made you a hero. Peace made you poor.

archetypes.title: The Matchmaker
archetypes.blurb: Eleven marriages arranged. Yours remains unwritten.

archetypes.title: The Fortune Hunter
archetypes.blurb: Charm is capital. You mean to invest it well.

stories.title: A Season of Masks
stories.premise: London, 1813. You arrive for the Season with a dazzling reputation, an empty purse, and one chance to secure your family's future — while a rival from your past threatens to expose everything.

stories.title: The Sunset Clause
stories.premise: You come home to sell your late grandmother's failing vineyard and get on with your city life. The only thing between you and a clean exit is the maddening owner of the rival winery next door — who holds the one contract that could save the place, or finish it.
stories.tone: Contemporary romance: warmth and banter, slow-burn tension, second chances with real stakes under the charm.
stories.question: Who's coming home?

archetypes.title: The Prodigal
archetypes.blurb: You left this town at eighteen and swore never to look back.

archetypes.title: The One Who Stayed
archetypes.blurb: Someone had to keep the lights on. It was always you.

archetypes.title: The Rival
archetypes.blurb: Business is business. Then they walked in.

archetypes.title: The Best Friend
archetypes.blurb: You've loved them quietly for years. Tonight the quiet ends.

archetypes.title: The Cynic
archetypes.blurb: Love is a story other people tell. You know better. Probably.

archetypes.title: The Second Chance
archetypes.blurb: You had them once and lost them. The universe is not subtle.

stories.title: The Enemy's Garden
stories.premise: Two kingdoms that have bled each other for a generation buy peace with a single promise: your hand, given to a stranger across the border you were raised to hate. You are expected to smile, to spy, and above all not to fall for the one person you're forbidden to trust.
stories.tone: Courtly fantasy romance: forbidden longing, political peril, oaths and secrets, a slow burn across enemy lines.
stories.question: Who is promised away?

archetypes.title: The Reluctant Betrothed
archetypes.blurb: Promised to a stranger to buy a fragile peace.

archetypes.title: The Enemy Prince
archetypes.blurb: You were meant to hate them. No one warned you they'd be kind.

archetypes.title: The Spymaster's Ward
archetypes.blurb: Sent to gather secrets. You didn't plan to lose your own.

archetypes.title: The Sworn Blade
archetypes.blurb: You guard their life. You were not asked to guard your heart.

archetypes.title: The Claimant
archetypes.blurb: This marriage restores your claim — and ruins the only thing you want.

archetypes.title: The Court Poet
archetypes.blurb: Both courts sing your verses. Neither knows you wrote the truth.
